prompt: The graph below shows the proportion of the population aged 65 and over in Japan, Sweden and the USA between 1980 and 2020, with projections to 2050.
model:
The line graph illustrates the percentage of people aged 65 or older in Japan, Sweden and the USA from 1980 to 2020, together with forecasts up to 2050.

Overall, the share of elderly people has risen and is expected to keep rising in all three countries. The most striking change is in Japan, which had the smallest proportion of older citizens in 1980 but is predicted to have by far the largest by 2050.

In 1980, 16% of Sweden's population was aged 65 or over, compared with 11% in the USA and 9% in Japan. Japan's figure then grew rapidly, drawing level with Sweden's at 17% in 2000 and reaching 29% in 2020. This upward trend is projected to continue, with the proportion expected to hit 38% by 2050, more than four times the 1980 level.

Sweden and the USA, by contrast, have seen much slower growth. The Swedish figure fluctuated between 16% and 18% until 2000 before rising gradually to 20% in 2020, and it is forecast to reach 24% by the middle of the century. In the USA, the proportion remained between 11% and 13% until 2010, then climbed to 17% in 2020; it is expected to stand at 22% in 2050, slightly below the figure for Sweden.
